newsitem.title: USA: Sears to revamp, add to automotive unit.
newsitem.headline: Sears to revamp, add to automotive unit.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Wednesday it will combine its off-mall tire stores under one brand name and add about 350 of those stores by the year 2000.
Sears also said it will spend $16 million in 1997 to remodel 105 off-mall tire stores in 1997.
The Sears tire group currently has 1,058 stores, including 161 NTW stores and 127 Tire America stores, which both operate outside of malls.

"We'll combine and convert (the off-mall tire stores) into one single name plate at the end of the first quarter this year," Paul Baffico, president of Sears auto stores, told analysts at a meeting here Wednesday. He would not divulge the name.
Sears tire group had $2.3 billion in revenues in 1996.
Sears also plans to open 73 new tire stores in 1997 and 100-125 new stores annually after, with a goal of reaching 1,400 stores by the year 2,000, he said.
Combining the off-mall tire stores under one name will allow Sears to have a national brand presence in that line, making it easier to advertise nationally, a spokesman said.
Sears' automotive parts store group will also undergo a transformation, consolidating many parts stores under the Parts America store name.
"We will open 100 new stores in '97 while concurrently converting 240 Western Auto stores," Baffico said.
Sears has 339 Western Auto stores and 288 Parts America stores. Some stores will retain the Western Auto name.

While some Western Auto Stores had service bays, Sears will focus on parts stores that will not offer automotive service, which are easier to open because of zoning and environmental reasons, a Sears spokesman said.
The parts group had $1.4 billion in revenue in 1996.
